transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-13 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Notes: kickoff + technical handoff for VPC/onboarding; mix of strategy and technical intake.

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Align on VPC peering steps, staging access, and initial pilot success criteria.
- Identify owners for runbook items and set cadence for performance testing.
- Confirm compliance asks (SOC2 scopes, KMS, audit logs).

[00:00] Priya Patel: alright everybody good afternoon, welcome, thanks for carving out time. this is Priya from Redwood, ae on the account. with me are Ethan, our csm, and Maya our se.
[00:10] Samir Rao: hey thanks Priya, yeah all good, Samir here. we've got Lena, Diego and Karen with me. big agenda for today is get us into the weeds on vpc peering and kickoff the onboarding runway.
[00:20] Priya Patel: perfect, i'll run quick context — halcyon signed the dedicated pilot last week and today's more of a technical kickstart: confirm networking, auth, staging access, and outline the first two sprint milestones. sound right?
[00:30] Lena Morales: yep that matches. we're aiming to have a small pilot handling real routing logs anonymized then expand. latency targets we talked about are sub-200ms p95 for 1k token prompts, cost matters too.
[00:40] Maya Singh: noted. for those numbers we'll want to run an initial perf baseline against the model variant you picked; we also need to know your typical sequence length and concurrency distribution so we can size pooling.
[00:50] Diego Park: concurrency peaks are about 30 req/s during batch window, outside that 3-5 rps. seq lengths usually 128 tokens avg, some longer outliers 600.
[01:05] Maya Singh: okay good. that explains why batching and kv cache will be important. quick question — do you plan to use Redwood Dedicated (reserved) or start on hosted then migrate?
[01:15] Karen Liu: we committed to the dedicated pilot per procurement, because we need isolation and predictable throughput. but we also want the option to fall back to hosted during maintenance windows.
[01:25] Priya Patel: that's a common pattern — we'll wire the routing policy so requests can route to a fallback hosted model during dedicated maintenance. Maya will document the fallback thresholds.
[01:34] Ethan Rossi: from a cs perspective i'll own the runbook and SLA checklist. i'll also coordinate the security questionnaire turnaround.
[01:40] Samir Rao: excellent. on security — we need to validate SOC2 scope, sso integration (saml), and KMS for key control. also audit logs retention.
[01:50] Maya Singh: we support SAML SSO via SSO provider, RBAC, and for private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. audit logging is configurable; retention can be set per tenant. i'll put the specific endpoints and log formats into the runbook.
[02:05] Lena Morales: on the vpc peering, we need the exact cidr ranges and if there are any NAT or firewall rules required. we prefer to do strict egress rules — minimize outbound reach.
[02:15] Priya Patel: understood. Diego, can you share your vpc ranges and whether you want an AWS privatelink or standard peering?
[02:22] Diego Park: we'd prefer privatelink if possible, because of cross-account restrictions. we can share account ids, the peering team will handle the rest.
[02:30] Maya Singh: Redwood supports privatelink for private deployments; there are a couple of extra steps on the sidecar for route tables. i'll capture step-by-step. note: privatelink has a slightly different NAT behavior which can affect egress ip visibility for KMS calls.
[02:45] Karen Liu: about kms — we want customer-managed keys for encrypting any logs we keep. can you confirm if that's available for the dedicated pilot?
[02:53] Maya Singh: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported; there are two integration patterns: 1) Redwood uses your customer KMS for storage encryption only, or 2) you supply keys and manage rotation via our KMS passthrough. pattern 2 needs a little more setup but gives you full control.
[03:10] Samir Rao: pattern 2 is preferred. what's the auth flow for the runtime to call KMS?
[03:16] Maya Singh: typically a cross-account role with short-lived credentials; we also have an option to bring your own HSM via private deployment if the compliance bar demands it.
[03:26] Lena Morales: okay noted. next: staging access — we need a service account and rootless keys so our devs can run smoke tests. what's the recommended provisioning path?
[03:36] Priya Patel: Ethan will create a staging workspace and provision api keys scoped to the environment. we'll give you a set of test keys and instructions. for service accounts we'll push a terraform module where you only fill in the vpc ids and account numbers.
[03:48] Diego Park: terraform module is great. can we get an example of the iam policy for the service account?
[03:52] Maya Singh: yes, i'll attach a minimal iam policy example in the runbook. note: for privatelink there's also a small trust policy change.
[04:00] Samir Rao: about metrics — we want token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards. are those available out of the box?
[04:08] Ethan Rossi: yes, the Redwood Console exposes per-route and per-model dashboards. i'll set up access for your analytics team. we can also push custom dashboards (grafana) via our observability api.
[04:18] Karen Liu: good. also want regression alerts tied to our eval-suite — if generation quality drops we need a notification.
[04:25] Maya Singh: Redwood Optimize supports quality monitoring and regression alerts. we'll want a small sample set of prompts and expected outputs to seed the evals.
[04:32] Priya Patel: action-wise, Maya will draft perf test plan; Ethan will draft runbook and console access; Diego to send vpc cidrs and decide on privatelink vs peering; Samir to confirm compliance point-of-contact.
[04:44] Lena Morales: quick note on data residency — part of our contract requires EU-only storage for some data. is that supported?
[04:50] Maya Singh: yes we can pin storage and runtime to EU regions for specific tenants; we'll need a clear mapping of datasets to residency requirements.
[04:58] Diego Park: ok we'll map that in a spreadsheet and share.
[05:02] Samir Rao: curious on typical onboarding timeline — from vpc peering to pilot run, what do you normally see?
[05:08] Priya Patel: for a dedicated pilot with privatelink usually 3-4 weeks: week 0 networking and access, week 1 perf baseline and smoke, week 2 pilot data runs and adjustments, week 3 ramp. could be faster if networking is trivial.
[05:20] Karen Liu: dependencies we have: security review, legal sign-off on data handling, and dev time for instrumentation.
[05:27] Ethan Rossi: will capture those in the runbook with owners. next meeting we propose is an se-led performance deep dive to walk through the baseline tests and map real traffic shapes.
[05:36] Maya Singh: for the deep dive i'll need sample payloads, expected latencies, and 24 hours of representative logs if possible.
[05:42] Diego Park: we can anonymize logs and share.
[05:45] Priya Patel: great. any blockers or concerns from the halcyon side?
[05:48] Lena Morales: main concern is unexpected egress costs during testing and making sure fallbacks don't degrade quality.
[05:54] Maya Singh: we'll include cost guardrails in the runbook and a clear fallback policy: rate-limit + model-variant downgrade, with alerting.
[06:02] Samir Rao: okay that helps. last thing — procurement asked about contract SLA language: can we get a redlined SLA for the dedicated pilot?
[06:09] Priya Patel: yes procurement will share a draft. i'll loop legal and your procurement. Ethan will follow up with timeline for redline.
[06:16] Ethan Rossi: i'll aim to get a draft response in 3 business days.
[06:19] Karen Liu: perfect.
[06:22] Priya Patel: quick recap so folks have clear owners — runbook + console access (Ethan), perf plan + sample payloads (Maya), vpc cidr and privatelink decision (Diego), compliance contact (Samir). we'll shoot to have those initial items done by 2026-01-20.
[06:40] Samir Rao: sounds good, appreciate the clarity.
[06:43] Priya Patel: thanks everyone. we'll send the runbook template and the terraform example right after this call and put calendar invite for the deep dive.
[06:50] Lena Morales: thanks all.
[06:52] Meeting end.
